title: The Summer Sun Shone Round Me
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
text_content:
THE summer sun shone round me,
The folded valley lay
In a stream of sun and odour,
That sultry summer day.

The tall trees stood in the sunlight
As still as still could be,
But the deep grass sighed and rustled
And bowed and beckoned me.

The deep grass moved and whispered
And bowed and brushed my face.
It whispered in the sunshine:
"The winter comes apace."
description: A sultry day in a folded valley, where the trees stand motionless and only the deep grass has something to say. Stevenson turns three short stanzas into a warning you feel on your skin.
